name: setup_github_repo
description: Local/dev-testing only -- one-time version-control bootstrap for a generated plugin: git init, write/merge .gitignore, first commit, create or link a GitHub remote, first push. Always creates or extends .gitignore BEFORE the first commit so .iox_env (setup_vscode_debug_config's file, holding the live PG3INIT MQTT credential) can never be committed, no matter what else is in the directory -- this is guaranteed in code, not something you need to remember each call. Idempotent: safe to call again later -- it skips git init if .git already exists, skips creating a remote if 'origin' is already configured, and reports committed: false with reason: 'no changes' instead of erroring when there's nothing new to commit. Remote setup has two paths: pass remote_url when the developer already created an empty repo themselves (on GitHub.com or elsewhere) and you just need to link it; otherwise this tries gh repo create automatically, and if the gh CLI isn't installed/authenticated on this host, it returns a non-fatal warning asking the developer to create an empty repo themselves and re-call with remote_url -- local init/commit still succeeded either way. Pushing is NOT gated in code -- always get the developer's explicit go-ahead before calling this at all (the first call already writes real history and, with push left true, creates a real remote repo and pushes to it), the same way you'd confirm before install_generated_plugin. For anything beyond this one-time setup -- git status/diff/log, stash/unstash, pull, later ad hoc commits outside this tool -- use run_shell_command directly with cwd set to the plugin's absolute_path; there's no need to come back to this tool for those.

location.description: The subdirectory name under the server's plugin output root -- the same 'location' generate_plugin_scaffold/install_generated_plugin use.

visibility.description: Visibility for a repo this tool creates via gh repo create. Ignored when remote_url is given (visibility is whatever the developer already chose). Defaults to private.

repo_name.description: Name for a repo this tool creates via gh repo create. Ignored when remote_url is given. Defaults to location.

remote_url.description: An existing, already-created (usually empty) repo's URL to link as 'origin' -- use this when the developer created the GitHub repo themselves, or when gh isn't available on this host. Omit to have this tool create one automatically via gh repo create.

commit_message.description: Commit message for this call's commit, if there are any changes to commit. Defaults to 'Initial commit'.

author_name.description: Git author/committer name for this call's commit. Ask the developer for their preferred name first; falls back to a generic default if omitted.

author_email.description: Git author/committer email for this call's commit. Ask the developer for their preferred email first; falls back to a generic default if omitted.

push.description: Whether to push after committing. Set false to only init/commit locally (and link remote_url, if given) without pushing anything. Defaults to true.
